newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Jan industry output seen up 4.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Jan industry output seen up 4.9 pct.

text.p: Figures on Japan's industrial output are expected to show a hefty 4.9 percent rise in January from a month earlier, an average of economists' forecasts showed.
The economists surveyed by Reuters predicted an increase of between 3.2 and 5.6 percent, against a modest 0.1 percent rise in December.
Industrial output data for January will be released by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) on Thursday.
A sharp increase in car production, backed by strong sales ahead of April's planned increase in the national sales tax, will be the main factor boosting overall output, economists said.
"Carmakers have stepped up production, expecting 'rush-in' demand ahead of the tax increase," said Yasushi Okuda, an economist with BZW Securities Japan.
Domestic vehicle production in January rose 19.3 percent from a year earlier.
"The car industry has a ripple effect on others. A rise in car production will lead to a rise in steel output, for instance," said Minako Iida, an economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Tokyo.
But economists stressed that the rise in car output was only temporary, supported by the heightened demand ahead of April's tax hike.
The government plans to raise the consumption tax from three percent to five percent from April 1.
Iida pointed out that production related to housing construction had already begun to fall as the pre-tax increase demand for houses seemed to have peaked out.
"We have to see whether the expected rise in production will lead to a pile up of inventories. It may end up depressing output in the April to June period," added BZW's Okuda.
